stories.headline: Allbirds rebrands as Smartbird AI infrastructure firm, hires ex-AWS exec as CEO; shares jump 30%+

key_facts.fact: Allbirds officially renamed itself Smartbird, Inc. on June 17, completing the sale of the Allbirds brand and footwear assets to American Exchange Group and pivoting fully to AI infrastructure.
Smartbird appointed Nadia Carlsten — former CEO of DCAI and ex-VP of product at Google spinoff SandboxAQ, who previously launched Amazon's quantum computing service at AWS — as president and CEO.
Smartbird shares (NASDAQ: BIRD) surged more than 30% on the news (some accounts cited nearly 60%); the stock was up about 25% YTD after Wednesday's move.
The company strengthened its balance sheet by increasing its convertible financing facility from $50 million to $100 million.

Smartbird said it provides AI infrastructure as a managed service to save upfront equipment costs for clients and is in active discussions with potential customers, designing its first cluster deployments.
Joe Vernachio resigned from the company and its board; Lily Yan Hughes was appointed board chair, and Annie Mitchell continues as CFO.

stories.headline: Tim Cook tells WSJ Apple price hikes are 'unavoidable' as AI-driven RAM shortage hits

key_facts.fact: Apple CEO Tim Cook told the Wall Street Journal that price increases for Apple products are 'unavoidable' because rising memory and storage chip costs have become 'unsustainable' to absorb.
Cook said the price of RAM has more than doubled since October 2025 and likened the memory shortage to a 'hundred-year flood' he hasn't seen in over 40 years.
Research firm TechInsights estimates Apple would need to raise the iPhone 18 Pro price by about $270 to maintain existing profit margins.
Cook said Apple would use cash reserves to help suppliers expand memory capacity but ruled out building Apple-owned memory or storage manufacturing facilities.
Cook is due to be replaced by John Ternus as Apple's CEO in September after 15 years in the role.
Memory chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are prioritizing high-bandwidth memory for AI servers over consumer-device chips, and shortages are expected to persist into 2027.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches first 'stacked' trio of AST SpaceMobile BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites

key_facts.fact: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral SLC-40 at 2:39 a.m. EDT on June 17 carrying BlueBird 8, 9 and 10 — the first time three BlueBirds were stacked in the same fairing.
Each Block 2 BlueBird carries a phased-array aperture roughly 2,400 square feet wide, designed to deliver up to ~200 Mbps directly to standard 4G/5G smartphones.
AST CEO Abel Avellan said BlueBirds 11-13 will ship shortly for the next launch and units through BlueBird 37 are already in active production at the company's 500,000-sq-ft Midland, Texas facility.
AST executives told investors they still target 45 BlueBirds in orbit this year despite losing BlueBird 7 to a Blue Origin New Glenn deployment error in late April.

stories.headline: AWS launches Continuum AI security agent and Context knowledge graph at NY Summit, citing Claude Mythos threat

key_facts.fact: AWS unveiled AWS Continuum, a gated-preview AI-native security service that discovers, prioritizes, validates and remediates code vulnerabilities at machine speed
AWS Continuum was framed as a response to Anthropic's Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models, which can chain software flaws into serious attacks faster than human defenders

AWS also launched AWS Context, a service that automatically builds an organizational knowledge graph from a company's existing data so agents can navigate business rules and domain knowledge at runtime

Continuum starts in a supervised 'learn mode' and earns autonomy only as customers grant permission category by category, reflecting AWS's design to maximize agent autonomy while keeping humans in control
Amazon S3 now lets customers attach up to 1 GB of mutable, queryable annotations directly to objects, purpose-built for AI agents and autonomous workflows

stories.headline: AI inference startup Baseten raising $1.5B in dual-tier deal at $11-13B valuation

key_facts.fact: Baseten is raising $1.5 billion in a dual-tiered deal, with some investors investing at an $11 billion valuation and others at a $13 billion valuation
The round more than doubles Baseten's $5 billion valuation set just three months earlier in a $300 million Series E led by IVP and CapitalG that included a $150 million anchor investment from NVIDIA
Baseten's annualized revenue reached $600 million at the end of Q1 2026, tripling from $200 million at the start of the quarter and up roughly 20x year-over-year
Baseten runs production inference workloads for AI-native customers including Cursor, Notion, Writer, Gamma, Descript, Clay and HeyGen
Baseten forecasts that inference will represent two-thirds of all AI compute demand by year-end 2026

stories.headline: Blackstone-led group takes Medallia from Thoma Bravo, sealing $5B PE wipeout

key_facts.fact: On June 17 Medallia announced a recapitalization that transfers ownership from Thoma Bravo to an investor group led by Blackstone, Apollo and FS KKR Capital Corp, with the new owners injecting $150M in fresh capital.
Thoma Bravo will lose the entire $5B it invested in Medallia's 2021 take-private (valued at $6.4B) — described by Verdad Advisers as the second-largest equity wipeout in PE history, behind only TXU.

The new ownership group were already Medallia's lenders, carrying loans at roughly 60-70 cents on the dollar; Thoma Bravo declined to inject capital when lenders sought more than $500M of additional equity.
Medallia plans to use the new capital plus an existing $500M commitment to accelerate AI-driven product development.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea warns record Samsung/SK Hynix bonuses risk fueling broader inflation

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea's 'Inflation Target Operation Status Review' report released on June 17 warned that exceptional performance bonuses at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, created by the semiconductor boom, are stimulating wage increase demands across manufacturing and services beyond the IT sector.
Special payments (performance bonuses) in the South Korean IT sector surged 60.6% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, while wage growth in non-IT sectors was just 2.1%.

Securities firms forecast Samsung Electronics' 2026 operating profit at about 350 trillion won ($295 billion) and SK Hynix's at 255 trillion won ($215 billion); Samsung memory division employees could receive average bonuses of 700 million won ($590,000) per person in Q1 2027, while SK Hynix employees receive about 750 million won ($633,000).

The BOK found that when bonus increases reach the top 10% of historical levels, fixed monthly pay in other industries rises an additional 0.02-0.03 percentage points, and consumer prices rise by 0.05 percentage points about five months later.

IT-sector bonuses contributed 1.3 percentage points to Q1 2026's 3.4% nominal wage growth — the 97th percentile of the 2012-2025 distribution — and the BOK projects this could exceed the 99th percentile in early 2027.

stories.headline: FDA approves AstraZeneca's Truqap as first targeted therapy for PTEN-deficient metastatic prostate cancer

key_facts.fact: On June 17 the FDA approved Truqap (capivasertib) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone for adults with PTEN-deficient metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve/sensitive prostate cancer.
The FDA simultaneously authorized the VENTANA PTEN (SP218) diagnostic assay to identify eligible patients with PTEN-deficient tumors.
Approval is based on the 1,012-patient CAPItello-281 trial, in which adding capivasertib reduced the risk of progression or death by 19%.
Median radiographic progression-free survival increased by 7.5 months in the trial, from 25.7 to 33.2 months.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.5-3.75% in Warsh debut; dot plot now sees rate hikes ahead

key_facts.fact: FOMC voted 12-0 to maintain the federal funds rate target range at 3.5%-3.75% on June 17, the first meeting led by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
The Fed cited elevated inflation tied in part to supply shocks including energy from the Middle East conflict; productivity and capital investment remain strong.
New dot plot shows nine of 18 voting members projecting at least one rate hike before year-end, with six projecting two 25-basis-point hikes.
Median projections see PCE inflation at 3.6% at year-end (up from 2.7% in March), real GDP at 2.2% (down from 2.4%), and unemployment at 4.3%.
After the decision, CME FedWatch showed odds of rates staying at 3.5-3.75% through year-end fell to 14.2% from 40.3% a day earlier, with markets repricing toward a December hike.

stories.headline: Frontier coalition commits $915M more to carbon removal; Anthropic joins Stripe, Google, Salesforce, H&M

key_facts.fact: On June 17 Frontier announced an additional $915M commitment to buy carbon removal credits, bringing its total advance market commitment (AMC) to $1.8B.
Anthropic and Salesforce joined the coalition as new participants alongside founding members Stripe, Google, Shopify and H&M Group.
The new funding targets ocean alkalinity enhancement, biomass-based removal, enhanced rock weathering and direct air capture; Frontier plans 10-15 offtake bets running as far as 2040.
Frontier launched in 2022 with a $1B AMC modeled on the global-health vaccine financing structure used for the pneumococcal vaccine.

stories.headline: Noam Shazeer leaves Google to lead OpenAI's architecture research, less than 2 years after $2.7B return

key_facts.fact: Noam Shazeer, Google VP of engineering and co-lead of Gemini, announced he is leaving Google to join OpenAI
OpenAI Chief Research Officer Mark Chen said Shazeer will serve as the company's new 'lead for architecture research'
Google rehired Shazeer in 2024 from Character.AI in a deal valued at approximately $2.7 billion; he then co-led Gemini's pretraining effort
Shazeer co-authored the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper that introduced the Transformer architecture underpinning ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude
The move comes as OpenAI prepares for an IPO and competes with Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta for elite researchers

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils ENPIRE: AI coding agents autonomously run robot training to 99% success without humans

key_facts.fact: Nvidia, Carnegie Mellon and UC Berkeley released ENPIRE, a closed-loop framework that lets AI coding agents reset physical scenes, run hardware trials, verify outcomes and rewrite policy code without human intervention between iterations
ENPIRE deployed 8 Codex coding agents on a fleet of 8 dual-arm YAM robot stations, each with its own hardware, GPU and token budget; agents coordinate by sharing code through Git
Agents reached 99% success on dexterous tasks including organizing pins into a pin box, seating GPUs and cutting zip ties
The system has 4 modules: Environment (auto-reset and verification), Policy Improvement, Rollout (parallel hardware trials), and Evolution (agents read research papers and revise training code)
The release coincided with Jensen Huang's VivaTech 2026 keynote in Paris, which featured physical AI as its central theme

stories.headline: Pew: 49% of US adults now use AI chatbots, up from 33% in 2024; ChatGPT leads but skepticism grows

key_facts.fact: 49% of US adults reported using AI chatbots in 2026, up from 33% in 2024, with 24% saying they use chatbots on a daily basis
44% of US adult chatbot users say they use ChatGPT, making it the dominant platform; Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI follow
Nearly two-thirds of Americans believe AI is advancing too quickly, and 40% believe AI will make society worse
Adoption of AI summaries and smart speakers is also rising but Americans' views on AI's societal impact are increasingly negative

stories.headline: French silicon-qubit startup Quobly raises €115M Series A to commercialize quantum on 300mm wafers

key_facts.fact: Quobly, spun out of France's CEA-Leti, raised €115 million in Series A funding to accelerate commercial development of silicon-based quantum computers, the company announced June 17.

The round was led by Bpifrance, Swiss security-chip maker SEALSQ, and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council Fund, Blast, ALIAD (Air Liquide's venture arm), and Innovacom; existing shareholders include CEA, CNRS, Quantonation, and Supernova Invest.

Quobly's approach builds qubits on the same 300-millimetre silicon wafers used by commercial chip fabs, leveraging FD-SOI technology and existing semiconductor supply chains rather than superconducting or trapped-ion designs.
Cloud access to Quobly's Alloy Pioneer system is targeted by the end of 2026; deployment into high-performance computing infrastructure is planned for 2027.

The round is one of the larger European silicon-qubit raises this year; Britain's Quantum Motion took $160 million in May, and the US Commerce Department awarded $2 billion in CHIPS Act funds to nine quantum companies in May, with IBM alone slated for $1 billion to build a domestic quantum foundry.

stories.headline: SandboxAQ signs $500M CHIPS R&D deal to develop semiconductor materials, cut foreign dependence

key_facts.fact: SandboxAQ announced on June 17 a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research and Development Office for a $500 million award to address foreign control of critical materials and chemistries used in semiconductor manufacturing.
The award funds development of novel molecules and formulations across four areas: PFAS-free process chemicals, catalysts, rare-earth-free magnets, and battery systems.
SandboxAQ will use the funding to enhance its ReAQT system and Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) to accelerate candidate-material screening using physics-based AI rather than lab trial-and-error.
SandboxAQ, an Alphabet spinoff, is backed by T. Rowe Price, Google, IQT, US Innovative Technology Fund, S32, Paladin Capital, Eric Schmidt, Breyer Capital, Ray Dalio, Marc Benioff, and Thomas Tull.

stories.headline: Sanders unveils American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act: 50% stock tax to seed ~$7T public fund

key_facts.fact: Senator Bernie Sanders shared the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act first to the AP on June 17, formalizing a previous proposal into legislation.
The bill would impose a one-time 50% stock tax (not cash) on AI companies that reach $200M in annual AI sales, including OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI.
Sanders estimates the fund would reach about $7 trillion and generate hundreds of billions annually for direct payments to Americans plus health, education and housing programs.
A seven-person commission, nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate, would manage the fund and exercise voting rights to block decisions harmful to the public.
A proposed 5% annual fund dividend would deliver direct payments of more than $1,000 to every American.

stories.headline: Trump announces Apple-Intel chip manufacturing deal; Intel stock jumps 9% premarket

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on June 18 that Apple had agreed to work with Intel to design and build its chips in the United States.
Intel shares jumped roughly 9% in premarket trading after the announcement.
The deal helps Apple diversify away from heavy reliance on TSMC, whose advanced production lines are in high demand from AI chipmakers like Nvidia and AMD.
Intel announced on June 16-17 at the VLSI Symposium in Honolulu that its 18A-P process node had entered risk production, an early proving stage.
Trump framed the agreement as the third major foundry customer win his administration has personally announced for Intel this year, following Nvidia and Tesla's TerraFab.
Neither company has confirmed specifics on which Apple chip lines would be made by Intel, what process node, or volume.

stories.headline: Trump confirms Apple will work with Intel to design and build chips in US; Intel jumps ~9% premarket

key_facts.fact: On June 18 Truth Social, Trump said Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and build its chips in the United States; Intel shares jumped about 9% in premarket trading.
Trump's post specifically said: 'Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build its Chips in America.' Apple shares gained 0.6%.
Apple is Intel's third major foundry win after Nvidia and Elon Musk's TeraFab, with Trump claiming credit for brokering all three.
Apple ditched Intel processors in 2020 for in-house Arm designs fabbed by TSMC; the new deal positions Intel Foundry as production partner for Apple-designed chips, not a return to Intel CPUs.
The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel last year for roughly $10B; that position has grown to be worth more than $50B.

stories.headline: White House demands Anthropic make Fable 5 guardrails uncircumventable; restriction tied to SK Telecom revocation

key_facts.fact: Trump administration officials told WIRED that if Anthropic wants to rerelease Fable 5, it will need to ensure the model's guardrails can't be circumvented
The White House move to restrict Mythos 5 came after it ordered Anthropic to revoke South Korea-based SK Telecom's access over alleged ties to China
Anthropic disabled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 with less than 90 minutes of notice; some staff openly questioned whether Trump is bullying the company
AI policy experts told WIRED that building model guardrails that cannot be circumvented may not be technically possible
JPMorgan Chase has stopped its staff in Hong Kong from accessing Anthropic's AI models, following a similar move by rival Goldman Sachs, the Financial Times reported
